gen-gf-mallanna-fs-literata: Tight-set sans letters up top, bookish serif below. Mallanna is at its best giving headings compact, open curves, while Literata, the text serif, is at its best carrying sentences with gentle stroke variation.
gen-gf-manjari-fs-literata: Wire-thin lines meet a pen-nib serif. Manjari's constant, straight-edged strokes against Literata's gently tilted, sturdy text serif make a sharp contrast, wire on one side and nib on the other.
gen-gf-margarine-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans keeps its lines unvarying and its c open like pincers, giving Margarine's big-lowercase display letters a steady partner. Smooth, plotter-like curves above, quiet uniformity underneath it all.
gen-gf-margarine-poppins: Margarine stands tall with its big lowercase and plotter-smooth lines, while Poppins follows with loose, rounded curves and no thick-thin flicker. Let Margarine go big and Poppins stay modest.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-bitter: Bitter reads grounded and dependable, with a very large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s. MedievalSharp stands over it, tall and bold, in a display voice.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans holds one unbroken line from end to end. Shrink MedievalSharp and its wide-mouthed letters stay crisp, though it still looks tallest and boldest next to the sans.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-poppins: Modern Poppins keeps its curves rope-loose and its lowercase tall, with no thick-thin flicker. But MedievalSharp is the much louder voice here, bold and commanding, still crisp when shrunk.
gen-gf-meera-inimai-fs-literata: Lockstep stems in Meera Inimai up top, then Literata's text serif follows with sturdy lines and gentle stress. Longer text would feel bookish and smooth, open-mouthed curves guiding the eye.
gen-gf-mina-fs-literata: Spaghetti-bold letters, then a measured, bookish serif. Mina's bold strokes never thicken or thin, which sets up a strong foil for Literata, the text serif whose contrast stays moderate.
gen-gf-mingzat-fs-literata: Literata brings sturdy, bookish serif lines to the table. Mingzat is best at approachable headings with a wide-open ring for its c, while Literata is best at narrowing strokes gently from stem to terminal.
